papers.title: UAV-Flow++: A Unified Suite for Benchmarking and Learning Language-Guided UAV Flight
papers.abstract: Language-guided UAV navigation has largely focused on long-horizon route planning, leaving short-range, object-relative flight maneuvers underexplored. To address this gap, we formulate Flying-on-a-Word (Flow), a task requiring a UAV to convert concise natural-language instruction, egocentric visual observation, and current state dynamics into continuous flight actions. Flow encompasses both primitive motion commands and complex object-interactive behaviors, assessing motion intent comprehension and spatial context grounding. To enable policy learning and closed-loop evaluation, we introduce UAV-Flow, a comprehensive dataset comprising 30,692 expert-piloted real-world trajectories across eight distinct motion categories, alongside 10,109 simulation trajectories in the UAV-Flow-Sim environment equipped with task-specific completion criteria. Furthermore, we develop FlowVLA, which undergoes imitation pretraining on mixed real-sim demonstrations and online post-training via Tail-Aware GRPO (TGRPO). By leveraging group reward distributions, TGRPO effectively reinforces high-reward action sequences. Evaluated on 273 held-out UAV-Flow-Sim episodes, pretrained FlowVLA achieves a mean success rate of 75.58%, outperforming the strongest baseline by 6.72 percentage points, which TGRPO post-training further elevates to 93.16% with superior sample efficiency. Physical UAV experiments demonstrate robust execution of object-relative commands in both indoor and outdoor real-world scenes. Together, Flow establishes a novel benchmark and learning framework for language-conditioned flight maneuvers.
papers.headline: 短い言葉でドローンを動かす、物体との位置関係に基づく飛行学習
papers.summary: 短い自然言語の指示に従い、物体との位置関係を踏まえてドローンを操縦する研究です。機体視点の画像と現在の運動状態から、連続的な飛行操作を生成します。実世界とシミュレーションの飛行データ、評価環境、学習手法を整備し、長距離の経路計画に比べて研究が少なかった近距離の飛行操作を扱います。
papers.advantages: 著者は、基本的な移動から物体に関わる複雑な操作までを扱う、共通の学習・評価基盤を提案しています。比較実験では、事前学習したFlowVLAの平均成功率が最も強い比較手法を6.72ポイント上回りました。追加学習による成功率向上と優れたサンプル効率も報告されています。ただし、比較手法の名前やサンプル効率の具体的な差は、arXivの概要には記載されていません。
papers.method: 言語指示、機体視点の画像、現在の運動状態を入力し、FlowVLAが連続的な飛行操作を出力します。まず実世界とシミュレーションの操縦例を混ぜ、手本の操作をまねる模倣学習を行います。その後、オンラインで追加学習するTGRPOを適用します。TGRPOは複数の行動列から得られる報酬の分布を利用し、高い報酬を得た行動列を重点的に強化する仕組みです。
papers.evaluation: データは8種類の動作を含む実世界の熟練操縦軌跡30,692件と、シミュレーション軌跡10,109件です。タスク別の完了条件を備えたUAV-Flow-Simで、学習に使わない273エピソードを評価しました。平均成功率は事前学習後に75.58%、TGRPOによる追加学習後に93.16%でした。屋内外の実機でも物体との位置関係に基づく指示の実行を示していますが、実機の試行数や成功率は記載されていません。
papers.futureWork: arXivの概要には今後の課題の記載がありません。未経験の指示や物体、環境にどこまで対応できるか、実機でどのような失敗が起きるかは、arXivの概要だけでは確認できません。これらは追加で確認すべき点であり、著者が明示した課題ではありません。

papers.title: Inner Product Regularization for Imitation Learning
papers.abstract: Robots that learn from demonstrations should extrapolate their policy despite state perturbations such as sensor noise, scene variation, and compounding errors. One approach to this robustness is regularization. Prior regularizers consider each state on its own and limit how sensitive the policy is to any perturbation at that state. By contrast, we explore how the policy's output shifts when given the same perturbation at different states. Our insight is that, locally, the robot should respond to state perturbations in a consistent manner: e.g., if changing an irrelevant object position does not impact the policy at one state, that same change should not shift the policy output at a nearby state. Applying this insight, we develop inner product regularization (InneR). We show that the inner product on action space induces an inner product on state space through the policy Jacobian (the Fisher information for stochastic policies), and that the null space of this inner product governs which state perturbations have a first-order effect on the policy. By clustering states whose inner products are aligned, averaging the inner products within each cluster, and minimizing the smallest eigenvalues of that average, InneR shapes the learned policy so that nearby states share a common null space. InneR enforces consistent responses to perturbations without limiting policy expressiveness, and can be appended to existing imitation learning pipelines for deterministic or stochastic policies. In simulated experiments, InneR makes learned policies more robust to irrelevant state dimensions and shifts between training and test distributions, whereas norm penalties often perform worse than behavior cloning. On a real robot arm performing three manipulation tasks, InneR raises the average success rate of a diffusion policy from 18% to 57% without additional data.
papers.headline: 状態の変化への反応をそろえ、模倣学習ロボットの頑健性を高める
papers.summary: 手本から動作を学ぶロボットが、センサー雑音や場面の変化で失敗しにくくなるようにする研究です。各状態で出力の変化を抑えるだけでなく、近い状態同士で同じ変化に一貫して反応するよう学習を調整します。提案手法InneRは、動作に無関係な状態の変化を共通して無視できる方策を目指します。
papers.advantages: 従来の正則化が各状態での変化への敏感さを個別に抑えるのに対し、InneRは状態間で反応をそろえます。著者は、行動を決める方策の表現力を制限せず、確定的・確率的な既存の模倣学習に追加できると主張しています。実験では、シミュレーションで頑健性が向上し、実機では追加データなしで平均成功率が18%から57%に上がったと報告されています。
papers.method: 方策の出力が状態の微小変化にどう反応するかを、ヤコビ行列という局所的な変化率で表します。これを用い、状態の変化同士の関係を測る内積を構成します。その内積が似た状態をまとめ、各群の内積を平均して小さい固有値を最小化します。これにより、出力に一次の影響を与えない変化の方向を近い状態間で共通化し、無関係な変化への一貫した反応を促します。
papers.evaluation: シミュレーションでは、動作に無関係な状態成分と、学習時・評価時のデータ分布の違いに対する頑健性を検証しています。変化の大きさを抑えるノルム罰則は、手本の行動を直接まねる行動クローニングより悪い場合が多かったと報告されています。実機のロボットアームでは3種類の操作課題を実施し、ノイズ除去を利用して行動を生成する拡散方策の平均成功率が18%から57%に向上しました。試行数や課題名は記載されていません。
papers.futureWork: arXivの概要には今後の課題の記載がありません。状態をまとめる際の設定への依存性、学習に必要な計算量、より多様な実機課題への適用範囲は、arXivの概要だけでは確認できません。これらは追加の確認事項であり、著者が述べた限界や今後の計画ではありません。

papers.title: An Integrated Architecture for Data-Efficient Real-Time Neural Imitation of Nonlinear Time-Optimal Model Predictive Control
papers.abstract: Nonlinear time-optimal model predictive control (TOMPC) enables highly performant control of constrained systems, but its computational cost prohibits real-time use on fast dynamical systems. Neural network imitation of the TOMPC control law can reduce online computational costs, yet existing work mostly targets quadratic cost formulations in simulation and addresses the challenges of neural controllers in isolation. This work imitates a long-horizon nonconvex TOMPC with hard terminal constraints, whose high computational cost limits training-data generation. We present (i) \emph{self-informed sampling (SIFS)}, a data-efficient expert-sampling strategy that uses a learned time-to-go to query the expert only where the policy deviates from time-optimal behavior, (ii) a complete training and control architecture that jointly addresses dataset correlation, suboptimal expert labels, covariate shift, constraint satisfaction and model mismatch, and (iii) real-world validation on a Furuta pendulum. SIFS matches standard dataset aggregation performance in roughly one-third of the training time and with less than half the training data. The resulting controller matches the region of attraction of the expert TOMPC while raising the control frequency from 1.4~Hz to 1~kHz. On hardware, the controller swings up and stabilizes the pendulum along trajectories closely matching the expert TOMPC solution.
papers.headline: 時間最適制御を少ない手本で学び、振り子の実時間制御を高速化
papers.summary: 制約を守りながら最短時間で目標に到達する制御は、計算が重く、高速な装置への適用が難しいという問題があります。本研究は、その制御をニューラルネットワークで模倣します。最適な動作から外れる場所を選んで手本を集める仕組みと、学習・制御を統合した構成により、少ないデータで高速な制御を実現します。
papers.advantages: 著者は、従来研究が主に二次形式の評価関数を用いたシミュレーションを扱い、学習制御の課題を個別に検討していたと位置づけています。本研究は、長い予測区間と厳密な終端制約を持つ、最適化が難しい時間最適制御を対象にします。比較では、標準的なデータ集約法と同等の性能を約3分の1の学習時間、半分未満の学習データで達成したと報告されています。
papers.method: 時間最適モデル予測制御は、先の動きを予測し、制約の下で到達時間を最小にする操作を計算します。提案するSIFSは、目標までの残り時間を学習して利用し、方策が時間最適な動作から外れる場所に限って、この計算で手本を取得します。高価な手本の生成を必要な場所に集中させる工夫です。さらに、データ間の相関、不十分な手本、状態分布のずれ、制約の順守、モデルと実機のずれを統合的に扱いますが、個別の対処方法は記載されていません。
papers.evaluation: SIFSを標準的なデータ集約法と比較し、学習時間と学習データ量を評価しています。得られた制御器は、元の時間最適制御と同じ吸引領域、つまり目標状態へ導ける初期状態の範囲を保ち、制御周波数を1.4Hzから1kHzへ高めたと報告されています。回転アームで振り子を動かすフルタ振り子の実機では、元の制御の解に近い軌道で振り上げと安定化を示しました。試行数や軌道誤差の数値は記載されていません。
papers.futureWork: arXivの概要には今後の課題の記載がありません。別の装置への適用範囲、モデルと実機のずれが大きい場合の性能、制約順守をどの範囲で保証できるかは、arXivの概要だけでは確認できません。これらは追加で確認すべき点であり、著者が明示した課題とは区別する必要があります。

papers.title: $π_0$: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control
papers.abstract: Robot learning holds tremendous promise to unlock the full potential of flexible, general, and dexterous robot systems, as well as to address some of the deepest questions in artificial intelligence. However, bringing robot learning to the level of generality required for effective real-world systems faces major obstacles in terms of data, generalization, and robustness. In this paper, we discuss how generalist robot policies (i.e., robot foundation models) can address these challenges, and how we can design effective generalist robot policies for complex and highly dexterous tasks. We propose a novel flow matching architecture built on top of a pre-trained vision-language model (VLM) to inherit Internet-scale semantic knowledge. We then discuss how this model can be trained on a large and diverse dataset from multiple dexterous robot platforms, including single-arm robots, dual-arm robots, and mobile manipulators. We evaluate our model in terms of its ability to perform tasks in zero shot after pre-training, follow language instructions from people and from a high-level VLM policy, and its ability to acquire new skills via fine-tuning. Our results cover a wide variety of tasks, such as laundry folding, table cleaning, and assembling boxes.
papers.headline: π₀：画像と言葉の知識を、多様なロボットの器用な操作へ
papers.summary: 多様な作業に対応するロボット学習で、データ不足や未知の状況への対応、動作の安定性が課題です。π₀は、事前学習済みの画像と言葉を扱うモデルを土台に、動作を生成する仕組みを組み合わせます。複数種類のロボットのデータで学び、洗濯物たたみなどの作業や、追加学習による新技能の獲得を評価します。
papers.advantages: 著者が狙う利点は、インターネット規模の学習で得た意味の知識を、ロボットの操作に生かすことです。単腕、双腕、移動しながら物を扱うロボットの多様なデータを利用する構成も示しています。ただし、arXivの概要には既存手法との比較条件や数値がなく、どの手法よりどれだけ優れるかは確認できません。
papers.method: 画像と言葉を扱う事前学習済みモデルの上に、フローマッチングという生成モデルの学習手法を使う構造を設けます。視覚と言語の情報をロボットの動作へ結び付け、複数のロボットから集めた大規模で多様なデータで学習します。既存の意味の知識を操作に活用する狙いです。入力の詳しい構成や動作の表現形式は、arXivの概要では説明されていません。
papers.evaluation: 事前学習後に対象作業の追加学習なしで動く能力、人や上位の画像・言語モデルによる方策からの言語指示に従う能力、追加学習で新技能を獲得する能力を評価しています。対象には洗濯物たたみ、テーブル清掃、箱の組み立てが含まれます。arXivの概要には、試行回数、成功率、比較手法、詳しい実験環境の記載はありません。
papers.futureWork: arXivの概要には今後の課題の記載がありません。データ、未知の状況への対応、動作の安定性は研究の背景として挙げられていますが、提案手法に残る具体的な限界や今後の計画は示されていません。

papers.title: Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware
papers.abstract: Fine manipulation tasks, such as threading cable ties or slotting a battery, are notoriously difficult for robots because they require precision, careful coordination of contact forces, and closed-loop visual feedback. Performing these tasks typically requires high-end robots, accurate sensors, or careful calibration, which can be expensive and difficult to set up. Can learning enable low-cost and imprecise hardware to perform these fine manipulation tasks? We present a low-cost system that performs end-to-end imitation learning directly from real demonstrations, collected with a custom teleoperation interface. Imitation learning, however, presents its own challenges, particularly in high-precision domains: errors in the policy can compound over time, and human demonstrations can be non-stationary. To address these challenges, we develop a simple yet novel algorithm, Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT), which learns a generative model over action sequences. ACT allows the robot to learn 6 difficult tasks in the real world, such as opening a translucent condiment cup and slotting a battery with 80-90% success, with only 10 minutes worth of demonstrations. Project website: https://tonyzhaozh.github.io/aloha/
papers.headline: 低価格の双腕ロボットで精密操作を学ぶ、動作列の模倣学習ACT
papers.summary: 精密な操作には高価なロボットやセンサーが必要になりがちです。この研究は、低価格の機器と独自の遠隔操作装置で集めた実演から、ロボットの動作を直接学びます。動作をひとまとまりの列として学ぶACTを提案し、少量の実演で電池の差し込みなどの実世界の作業に取り組みます。
papers.advantages: 著者が示す利点は、低価格で精度に限りのある機器でも、人の実演から細かな操作を学べることです。動作の誤差が時間とともに積み重なる問題や、実演の振る舞いが一定でない問題に対処するため、動作列を学びます。arXivの概要には実世界での成功率が示されていますが、既存手法との比較結果や機器の具体的な価格はありません。
papers.method: 独自の遠隔操作装置で実際の作業の実演を集め、実演から動作をまねる模倣学習を行います。中心となるACTは、系列データを扱うニューラルネットワークのTransformerを使い、複数の動作をひとまとまりにした動作列の生成モデルを学びます。この工夫で誤差の蓄積などに対処します。観測入力の詳しい構成や、生成した動作列の実行方法はarXivの概要では確認できません。
papers.evaluation: 実世界の難しい操作6課題で検証しています。例として、半透明の調味料容器を開ける作業と、電池を差し込む作業が挙げられています。arXivの概要は、10分相当の実演で80〜90％の成功率を報告しています。ただし、課題別の成功率、試行回数、実演時間の課題ごとの配分、比較手法の結果は明記されていません。

papers.title: $π_{0.5}$: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization
papers.abstract: In order for robots to be useful, they must perform practically relevant tasks in the real world, outside of the lab. While vision-language-action (VLA) models have demonstrated impressive results for end-to-end robot control, it remains an open question how far such models can generalize in the wild. We describe $π_{0.5}$, a new model based on $π_{0}$ that uses co-training on heterogeneous tasks to enable broad generalization. $π_{0.5}$\ uses data from multiple robots, high-level semantic prediction, web data, and other sources to enable broadly generalizable real-world robotic manipulation. Our system uses a combination of co-training and hybrid multi-modal examples that combine image observations, language commands, object detections, semantic subtask prediction, and low-level actions. Our experiments show that this kind of knowledge transfer is essential for effective generalization, and we demonstrate for the first time that an end-to-end learning-enabled robotic system can perform long-horizon and dexterous manipulation skills, such as cleaning a kitchen or bedroom, in entirely new homes.
papers.headline: π₀.₅：異なるデータを一緒に学び、初めての家でも長い作業へ
papers.summary: 実験室の外や未知の家でも役立つロボットを目指し、π₀を基にしたπ₀.₅を提案します。画像・言語・動作を結び付けるモデルに、複数ロボットのデータやウェブ由来の情報などを共同で学習させます。異なる情報源の知識を操作に生かし、初めての家で台所や寝室を片付けるような長い作業を実演します。

papers.title: High-Dimensional Continuous Control Using Generalized Advantage Estimation
papers.abstract: Policy gradient methods are an appealing approach in reinforcement learning because they directly optimize the cumulative reward and can straightforwardly be used with nonlinear function approximators such as neural networks. The two main challenges are the large number of samples typically required, and the difficulty of obtaining stable and steady improvement despite the nonstationarity of the incoming data. We address the first challenge by using value functions to substantially reduce the variance of policy gradient estimates at the cost of some bias, with an exponentially-weighted estimator of the advantage function that is analogous to TD(lambda). We address the second challenge by using trust region optimization procedure for both the policy and the value function, which are represented by neural networks. Our approach yields strong empirical results on highly challenging 3D locomotion tasks, learning running gaits for bipedal and quadrupedal simulated robots, and learning a policy for getting the biped to stand up from starting out lying on the ground. In contrast to a body of prior work that uses hand-crafted policy representations, our neural network policies map directly from raw kinematics to joint torques. Our algorithm is fully model-free, and the amount of simulated experience required for the learning tasks on 3D bipeds corresponds to 1-2 weeks of real time.

papers.title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control
papers.abstract: We study how vision-language models trained on Internet-scale data can be incorporated directly into end-to-end robotic control to boost generalization and enable emergent semantic reasoning. Our goal is to enable a single end-to-end trained model to both learn to map robot observations to actions and enjoy the benefits of large-scale pretraining on language and vision-language data from the web. To this end, we propose to co-fine-tune state-of-the-art vision-language models on both robotic trajectory data and Internet-scale vision-language tasks, such as visual question answering. In contrast to other approaches, we propose a simple, general recipe to achieve this goal: in order to fit both natural language responses and robotic actions into the same format, we express the actions as text tokens and incorporate them directly into the training set of the model in the same way as natural language tokens. We refer to such category of models as vision-language-action models (VLA) and instantiate an example of such a model, which we call RT-2. Our extensive evaluation (6k evaluation trials) shows that our approach leads to performant robotic policies and enables RT-2 to obtain a range of emergent capabilities from Internet-scale training. This includes significantly improved generalization to novel objects, the ability to interpret commands not present in the robot training data (such as placing an object onto a particular number or icon), and the ability to perform rudimentary reasoning in response to user commands (such as picking up the smallest or largest object, or the one closest to another object). We further show that incorporating chain of thought reasoning allows RT-2 to perform multi-stage semantic reasoning, for example figuring out which object to pick up for use as an improvised hammer (a rock), or which type of drink is best suited for someone who is tired (an energy drink).

papers.title: ORB-SLAM3: An Accurate Open-Source Library for Visual, Visual-Inertial and Multi-Map SLAM
papers.abstract: This paper presents ORB-SLAM3, the first system able to perform visual, visual-inertial and multi-map SLAM with monocular, stereo and RGB-D cameras, using pin-hole and fisheye lens models. The first main novelty is a feature-based tightly-integrated visual-inertial SLAM system that fully relies on Maximum-a-Posteriori (MAP) estimation, even during the IMU initialization phase. The result is a system that operates robustly in real-time, in small and large, indoor and outdoor environments, and is 2 to 5 times more accurate than previous approaches. The second main novelty is a multiple map system that relies on a new place recognition method with improved recall. Thanks to it, ORB-SLAM3 is able to survive to long periods of poor visual information: when it gets lost, it starts a new map that will be seamlessly merged with previous maps when revisiting mapped areas. Compared with visual odometry systems that only use information from the last few seconds, ORB-SLAM3 is the first system able to reuse in all the algorithm stages all previous information. This allows to include in bundle adjustment co-visible keyframes, that provide high parallax observations boosting accuracy, even if they are widely separated in time or if they come from a previous mapping session. Our experiments show that, in all sensor configurations, ORB-SLAM3 is as robust as the best systems available in the literature, and significantly more accurate. Notably, our stereo-inertial SLAM achieves an average accuracy of 3.6 cm on the EuRoC drone and 9 mm under quick hand-held motions in the room of TUM-VI dataset, a setting representative of AR/VR scenarios. For the benefit of the community we make public the source code.

papers.title: Back to Pixels: Lifting Latent Video Diffusion into Pixel Space
papers.abstract: Frontier video generation models work in a VAE latent space that compresses video in both space and time. This compression made training tractable, but now limits high-resolution, controllable, and interactive generation -- doubling resolution quadruples token count, conditions apply to groups of frames rather than individual ones, and each response must wait for the rest of its multi-frame block. We present PixVid, a simple yet effective method that lifts a pretrained latent video model to directly generate every frame in pixel space. PixVid keeps the diffusion transformer and replaces the VAE decoder with a convolutional head that renders its outputs into pixels. We find that predicting clean video rather than velocity, together with a larger noise shift, is key to quality. Finetuned from Wan2.1-14B, PixVid is competitive with the latent baseline within $\sim 1.3$M training clips. Working framewise in pixels, it generates at $2\times$ higher resolution with the same per-frame token count, keeps depth-conditioned video editing aligned under fast motion, and responds to each action at the next frame. Project page: https://chenshuo20.github.io/PixVid/

papers.title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
papers.abstract: How multimodal language models should encode visual input remains up for debate. Most models use a pretrained vision encoder, while some recent recipes train the encoder from scratch with the language model or remove it entirely. Vision encoders bundle together three design choices: a visual prior from upstream pretraining, dedicated vision capacity, and pre-fusion placement of that capacity (i.e., before the multimodal backbone). Because published models also differ in data, architecture, and compute, comparing them cannot isolate the effect of each choice. We disentangle these choices via a controlled framework where we pretrain all models from scratch on common data and compare them on visual question answering and language benchmarks at matched lifetime compute. We find that the visual prior is not necessary; an encoder trained jointly from scratch is on par with a pretrained one, without a separate training stage. What matters instead is dedicated vision capacity: an encoder-free model trails on visual understanding even when its backbone is enlarged by the encoder's parameter count. Yet that capacity need not precede multimodal fusion, as vision-only modules added in-fusion to early backbone layers perform comparably to a pre-fusion encoder and can lower time to first token. These results also hold across backbone sizes, when encoder pretraining is treated as free, and when starting from a pretrained language model. Overall, our findings favor dedicated vision capacity trained jointly with the backbone and placed early within it.

papers.title: TTB: Test-time Baking for Efficient Rendering of Decoder-only View Synthesis Models
papers.abstract: Decoder-only Large View Synthesis Models (LVSMs) with KV-cache have recently achieved state-of-the-art quality by regressing novel views from neural networks without reconstructing 3D geometry, while Test-Time Training (TTT) layers save computation but sacrifice quality. We propose Test-Time Baking (TTB), a strategy that learns to bake global scene information from cross-view attention into a lightweight MLP, enabling fast and high-fidelity novel-view decoding. The first key is to repurpose the fast-weight MLP of TTT to learn the cross-view attention mapping explicitly from its input-output pairs, rather than replacing attention entirely, achieving the same rendering efficiency as TTT while delivering substantially higher quality. The second key addresses a modality misalignment between context prefilling and novel-view rendering: we disentangle context tokens into camera-only context rendering tokens to serve as TTB input, and context ground-truth tokens with image content to serve as the TTB mapping target, ensuring the baked MLPs are relieved of the modality generalization challenge between context and novel-view processing. Our method achieves up to **23x** rendering speedup with quality on par with the state-of-the-art across several benchmarks. Project page: https://test-time-baking.github.io

papers.summary: 複数の画像から別の視点の画像を生成するモデルでは、高品質な処理の計算負担が課題です。TTBは、視点間の情報を参照する処理を小型ネットワークに学習させ、生成時に利用します。参照画像を処理するときと新しい視点を描くときの入力の違いにも対処し、品質を保ちながら描画を高速化する研究です。

papers.title: Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition
papers.abstract: In this work we investigate the effect of the convolutional network depth on its accuracy in the large-scale image recognition setting. Our main contribution is a thorough evaluation of networks of increasing depth using an architecture with very small (3x3) convolution filters, which shows that a significant improvement on the prior-art configurations can be achieved by pushing the depth to 16-19 weight layers. These findings were the basis of our ImageNet Challenge 2014 submission, where our team secured the first and the second places in the localisation and classification tracks respectively. We also show that our representations generalise well to other datasets, where they achieve state-of-the-art results. We have made our two best-performing ConvNet models publicly available to facilitate further research on the use of deep visual representations in computer vision.

papers.title: Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks
papers.abstract: State-of-the-art object detection networks depend on region proposal algorithms to hypothesize object locations. Advances like SPPnet and Fast R-CNN have reduced the running time of these detection networks, exposing region proposal computation as a bottleneck. In this work, we introduce a Region Proposal Network (RPN) that shares full-image convolutional features with the detection network, thus enabling nearly cost-free region proposals. An RPN is a fully convolutional network that simultaneously predicts object bounds and objectness scores at each position. The RPN is trained end-to-end to generate high-quality region proposals, which are used by Fast R-CNN for detection. We further merge RPN and Fast R-CNN into a single network by sharing their convolutional features---using the recently popular terminology of neural networks with 'attention' mechanisms, the RPN component tells the unified network where to look. For the very deep VGG-16 model, our detection system has a frame rate of 5fps (including all steps) on a GPU, while achieving state-of-the-art object detection accuracy on PASCAL VOC 2007, 2012, and MS COCO datasets with only 300 proposals per image. In ILSVRC and COCO 2015 competitions, Faster R-CNN and RPN are the foundations of the 1st-place winning entries in several tracks. Code has been made publicly available.

papers.title: Tactile Sensors Are an Effective Substitute for Wrist Cameras in Contact-Rich or Occluded Manipulation
papers.abstract: Learned manipulation policies often rely on wrist-mounted cameras for close-range visual feedback that complements external views of the workspace. However, contact-rich manipulation requires establishing and maintaining contacts that can remain hidden even from wrist cameras. Tactile sensors mounted on fingers can reliably and directly measure contact, without needing visual access. In this work, we show that this feedback enables policies to recover the performance advantage of wrist cameras using scene and egocentric vision together with touch. Our approach incorporates two low-cost tactile arrays into a visuotactile ACT policy, without wrist images during training or deployment. We evaluate six real-world task families spanning placement, insertion, occluded retrieval, and sustained-contact tool use. On three contact-rich tasks, we independently vary wrist-camera and tactile availability while keeping the demonstrations, policy architecture, and optimization settings fixed. Adding wrist cameras improves success by 18.3-28.3 percentage points over vision without wrist images. Adding tactile sensing instead improves success by 31.7-60.0 percentage points and yields higher observed success than vision-only policies with wrist cameras on all three tasks, with significant advantages on two under Holm-corrected tests. These results support finger-mounted tactile sensing as an effective alternative to wrist cameras in the evaluated contact-rich settings.

papers.title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
papers.abstract: Tactile sensing is an indispensable modality for contact-rich dexterous manipulation, a capability that hints at the ultimate frontiers of embodied intelligence. However, commercially available tactile sensors are still at a relatively early stage of development, with each type of sensor offering irreplaceable strengths alongside its own drawbacks. A key challenge is thus to free tactile understanding from sensor-specific physics, so that embodied models can effectively leverage heterogeneous tactile data. To this end, we develop LingBot-Touch, a tactile foundation model characterized by the following properties. (i) Our model yields a unified representation across different tactile sensors (i.e., piezoresistive, magnetic, and visuotactile sensors), and is easily extensible to new sensor types. (ii) The resulting tactile tokens are plug-and-play: they can be seamlessly integrated into policy models across paradigms, from diffusion policy to vision-language-action (VLA) models such as $π_{0.5}$ and LingBot-VLA, consistently enhancing manipulation dexterity. (iii) Extensive experiments, spanning simulation and real-robot deployments across multiple hardware platforms, demonstrate that our tactile representation substantially benefits complex manipulation tasks while maintaining strong computational efficiency. We believe the findings in this work demonstrate the potential of leveraging cross-sensor data to scale tactile learning, and offer encouraging insights for the design of future hardware and embodied models.

papers.title: VLA Adaptation with Real and Simulated Data: A Case Study on Robotic Chess
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are trained as general-purpose foundation models for robot learning, and require fine-tuning for each downstream task and robot. This raises practical questions such as how much data and training updates are needed, how checkpoints should be selected, and whether simulation can be leveraged to alleviate the cost of real data collection. We study these questions on a task that requires both precise manipulation and spatial understanding of the scene. In this task, an SO-101 arm moves a chess king between two squares that are given only by their names, such as e4 and a5. We fine-tune $π_{0.5}$ with various dataset sizes and update budgets, using teleoperated demonstrations as well as simulated demonstrations from a randomized scripted expert that imitates the variability of human demonstrations. In simulation, the success rate scales with both data and updates. Importantly, we find that a short learning-rate cool-down adds up to 31 points and is necessary for comparing checkpoints, and that validation loss and action error are unreliable for model selection. On the real arm, we fine-tune on up to 256 teleoperated demonstrations and evaluate ten policies in 25 trials each. Partial results indicate that pretraining on the simulated demonstrations helps substantially, most clearly when real data is scarce. We also present a negative result, in which training on the policy's own rollouts with filtered behavior cloning, RECAP-style advantage conditioning, corrections from an automatic coach, or residual reinforcement learning did not yield a measurable improvement over plain behavior cloning in our setting. We release the simulator, the expert and the real demonstrations.

papers.title: Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Action Diffusion
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Diffusion Policy, a new way of generating robot behavior by representing a robot's visuomotor policy as a conditional denoising diffusion process. We benchmark Diffusion Policy across 12 different tasks from 4 different robot manipulation benchmarks and find that it consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art robot learning methods with an average improvement of 46.9%. Diffusion Policy learns the gradient of the action-distribution score function and iteratively optimizes with respect to this gradient field during inference via a series of stochastic Langevin dynamics steps. We find that the diffusion formulation yields powerful advantages when used for robot policies, including gracefully handling multimodal action distributions, being suitable for high-dimensional action spaces, and exhibiting impressive training stability. To fully unlock the potential of diffusion models for visuomotor policy learning on physical robots, this paper presents a set of key technical contributions including the incorporation of receding horizon control, visual conditioning, and the time-series diffusion transformer. We hope this work will help motivate a new generation of policy learning techniques that are able to leverage the powerful generative modeling capabilities of diffusion models. Code, data, and training details is publicly available diffusion-policy.cs.columbia.edu

papers.title: Domain Randomization for Transferring Deep Neural Networks from Simulation to the Real World
papers.abstract: Bridging the 'reality gap' that separates simulated robotics from experiments on hardware could accelerate robotic research through improved data availability. This paper explores domain randomization, a simple technique for training models on simulated images that transfer to real images by randomizing rendering in the simulator. With enough variability in the simulator, the real world may appear to the model as just another variation. We focus on the task of object localization, which is a stepping stone to general robotic manipulation skills. We find that it is possible to train a real-world object detector that is accurate to $1.5$cm and robust to distractors and partial occlusions using only data from a simulator with non-realistic random textures. To demonstrate the capabilities of our detectors, we show they can be used to perform grasping in a cluttered environment. To our knowledge, this is the first successful transfer of a deep neural network trained only on simulated RGB images (without pre-training on real images) to the real world for the purpose of robotic control.

papers.title: OpenVLA: An Open-Source Vision-Language-Action Model
papers.abstract: Large policies pretrained on a combination of Internet-scale vision-language data and diverse robot demonstrations have the potential to change how we teach robots new skills: rather than training new behaviors from scratch, we can fine-tune such vision-language-action (VLA) models to obtain robust, generalizable policies for visuomotor control. Yet, widespread adoption of VLAs for robotics has been challenging as 1) existing VLAs are largely closed and inaccessible to the public, and 2) prior work fails to explore methods for efficiently fine-tuning VLAs for new tasks, a key component for adoption. Addressing these challenges, we introduce OpenVLA, a 7B-parameter open-source VLA trained on a diverse collection of 970k real-world robot demonstrations. OpenVLA builds on a Llama 2 language model combined with a visual encoder that fuses pretrained features from DINOv2 and SigLIP. As a product of the added data diversity and new model components, OpenVLA demonstrates strong results for generalist manipulation, outperforming closed models such as RT-2-X (55B) by 16.5% in absolute task success rate across 29 tasks and multiple robot embodiments, with 7x fewer parameters. We further show that we can effectively fine-tune OpenVLA for new settings, with especially strong generalization results in multi-task environments involving multiple objects and strong language grounding abilities, and outperform expressive from-scratch imitation learning methods such as Diffusion Policy by 20.4%. We also explore compute efficiency; as a separate contribution, we show that OpenVLA can be fine-tuned on consumer GPUs via modern low-rank adaptation methods and served efficiently via quantization without a hit to downstream success rate. Finally, we release model checkpoints, fine-tuning notebooks, and our PyTorch codebase with built-in support for training VLAs at scale on Open X-Embodiment datasets.

papers.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
papers.abstract: We propose a new family of policy gradient methods for reinforcement learning, which alternate between sampling data through interaction with the environment, and optimizing a "surrogate" objective function using stochastic gradient ascent. Whereas standard policy gradient methods perform one gradient update per data sample, we propose a novel objective function that enables multiple epochs of minibatch updates. The new methods, which we call proximal policy optimization (PPO), have some of the benefits of trust region policy optimization (TRPO), but they are much simpler to implement, more general, and have better sample complexity (empirically). Our experiments test PPO on a collection of benchmark tasks, including simulated robotic locomotion and Atari game playing, and we show that PPO outperforms other online policy gradient methods, and overall strikes a favorable balance between sample complexity, simplicity, and wall-time.

papers.title: ORB-SLAM: a Versatile and Accurate Monocular SLAM System
papers.abstract: This paper presents ORB-SLAM, a feature-based monocular SLAM system that operates in real time, in small and large, indoor and outdoor environments. The system is robust to severe motion clutter, allows wide baseline loop closing and relocalization, and includes full automatic initialization. Building on excellent algorithms of recent years, we designed from scratch a novel system that uses the same features for all SLAM tasks: tracking, mapping, relocalization, and loop closing. A survival of the fittest strategy that selects the points and keyframes of the reconstruction leads to excellent robustness and generates a compact and trackable map that only grows if the scene content changes, allowing lifelong operation. We present an exhaustive evaluation in 27 sequences from the most popular datasets. ORB-SLAM achieves unprecedented performance with respect to other state-of-the-art monocular SLAM approaches. For the benefit of the community, we make the source code public.

papers.title: ORB-SLAM2: an Open-Source SLAM System for Monocular, Stereo and RGB-D Cameras
papers.abstract: We present ORB-SLAM2 a complete SLAM system for monocular, stereo and RGB-D cameras, including map reuse, loop closing and relocalization capabilities. The system works in real-time on standard CPUs in a wide variety of environments from small hand-held indoors sequences, to drones flying in industrial environments and cars driving around a city. Our back-end based on bundle adjustment with monocular and stereo observations allows for accurate trajectory estimation with metric scale. Our system includes a lightweight localization mode that leverages visual odometry tracks for unmapped regions and matches to map points that allow for zero-drift localization. The evaluation on 29 popular public sequences shows that our method achieves state-of-the-art accuracy, being in most cases the most accurate SLAM solution. We publish the source code, not only for the benefit of the SLAM community, but with the aim of being an out-of-the-box SLAM solution for researchers in other fields.

papers.title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
papers.abstract: Foundation models pretrained on large natural-image collections are increasingly adapted for medical image segmentation, in the expectation that they will replace models trained for each task. Most comparisons, however, use data from the training distribution and a single task-specific baseline whose configuration is rarely justified, and therefore provide limited evidence of performance at new clinical sites. It also remains unclear how much of a foundation model must be adapted, and what determines this. We adapted a foundation model, DINOv2, with strategies ranging from tuning only its bias terms to full fine-tuning, and compared it with U-Nets and ResU-Nets trained from scratch. Experiments covered colonoscopy, breast ultrasound and dermoscopy, with testing on held-out data from the training source and on independent datasets from other institutions. The adapted foundation model generalised better on every external dataset. Within the training distribution, the task-specific models remained competitive when training data were abundant, and delineated boundaries more precisely, while the foundation model more often missed small lesions. Only a small fraction of the foundation model required adaptation, and the capacity needed was determined by the imaging domain rather than by the adaptation method. A widely used polyp test set was also found to duplicate images from another benchmark. Foundation-model adaptation is therefore warranted where models must work across sites, with capacity selected on the target domain.

papers.title: Toward Foundation Detection Models via Example-Based Grounding in EM-DETR
papers.abstract: DeepLearning (DL)-based Computer-Aided Diagnostic (CAD) systems have shown great promise in supporting clinicians, but their performance heavily depends on the availability of large, well-annotated datasets. In medical lesion detection, the scarcity of comprehensive, stan dardized annotations and the heterogeneity of existing datasets limit the development of robust foundation models. In this work, we introduce a novel approach to building a multi-domain foundation model for le sion detection by integrating diverse medical image datasets annotated for both anatomical structures and abnormalities. We first propose a student-teacher training strategy to effectively combine datasets with heterogeneous label spaces, mitigating catastrophic forgetting, and im proving feature learning. In addition, building on our previously pro posed example-based EM-DETR framework, we adapt it to jointly learn from multiple domain-specific datasets, enabling fine-grained, example driven detection across modalities. Our model achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) results, with image-level AUC scores exceeding previous SOTA by 1% point on four key findings in CXRs. We achieve a leading mAP50 in CXRs and mammography, surpassing EM-DETR trained on a single dataset by 2-3% points. This approach paves the way for scalable foundation models in medical imaging that leverage heterogeneous data while maintaining robust and generalizable performance.

papers.title: TorchCurves: Differentiable Parametric Curves
papers.abstract: We present TorchCurves, a PyTorch library that treats vector-valued parametric curves as learnable primitives. Its central operation maps batches of scalar inputs to points on curves represented in B-spline or Legendre polynomial bases, with differentiation through both inputs and coefficients. Curve coefficients can be optimized jointly with the surrounding model or produced by another network. The library provides trainable modules, reusable basis modules, and a functional interface, supporting applications ranging from continuous feature embeddings to Kolmogorov-Arnold networks and functional regression. Its implementation combines classical evaluation algorithms with vectorized PyTorch operations, emphasizing readability and maintainability without custom hardware kernels. Timing experiments compare curve evaluation against NumPy and SciPy and KAN training against EfficientKAN across a range of problem sizes. The results illustrate where this generality remains computationally practical and where overhead is substantial. Library is available on GitHub at https://github.com/alexshtf/torchcurves.

papers.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
papers.abstract: Deeper neural networks are more difficult to train. We present a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used previously. We explicitly reformulate the layers as learning residual functions with reference to the layer inputs, instead of learning unreferenced functions. We provide comprehensive empirical evidence showing that these residual networks are easier to optimize, and can gain accuracy from considerably increased depth. On the ImageNet dataset we evaluate residual nets with a depth of up to 152 layers---8x deeper than VGG nets but still having lower complexity. An ensemble of these residual nets achieves 3.57% error on the ImageNet test set. This result won the 1st place on the ILSVRC 2015 classification task. We also present analysis on CIFAR-10 with 100 and 1000 layers. The depth of representations is of central importance for many visual recognition tasks. Solely due to our extremely deep representations, we obtain a 28% relative improvement on the COCO object detection dataset. Deep residual nets are foundations of our submissions to ILSVRC & COCO 2015 competitions, where we also won the 1st places on the tasks of ImageNet detection, ImageNet localization, COCO detection, and COCO segmentation.

papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.abstract: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks in an encoder-decoder configuration. The best performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train. Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including ensembles by over 2 BLEU. On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of the best models from the literature. We show that the Transformer generalizes well to other tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing both with large and limited training data.
papers.headline: 注意機構だけで系列を処理するTransformer、翻訳品質と学習効率を向上

papers.advantages: 従来の主流モデルが使う再帰処理や畳み込みを取り除き、注意機構だけに基づく構成にした点が特徴です。著者は構造の単純さを掲げています。二つの翻訳課題では、品質の優位性に加え、並列処理のしやすさと学習時間の短縮を報告しています。英独翻訳では複数モデルを組み合わせた既存結果も上回り、英仏翻訳では単一モデルとして当時の最高性能を達成したとしています。
papers.method: 入力系列を内部表現へ変換するエンコーダーと、その表現から出力系列を生成するデコーダーを使います。中心は、必要な情報を関連性に応じて参照する注意機構です。従来のような再帰処理や畳み込みに頼らない構成が、並列処理と学習時間の短縮につながるとしています。入力文から翻訳文を得る用途に加え、英文の句や節のまとまりを求める構成素解析にも適用しています。内部の計算手順の詳細はarXivの概要にありません。
papers.evaluation: 翻訳評価指標BLEUで、WMT 2014の英独翻訳は28.4を記録し、複数モデルの組み合わせを含む既存最高結果を2点超上回りました。英仏翻訳は単一モデルで41.8を記録しています。後者の学習は、画像処理などに用いる並列計算装置GPUを8基使い、3.5日でした。英文の構成素解析にも、大規模な学習データと限られた学習データの両条件で適用しましたが、解析の数値結果はarXivの概要にありません。

papers.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
papers.abstract: We introduce a new language representation model called BERT, which stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. Unlike recent language representation models, BERT is designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers. As a result, the pre-trained BERT model can be fine-tuned with just one additional output layer to create state-of-the-art models for a wide range of tasks, such as question answering and language inference, without substantial task-specific architecture modifications. BERT is conceptually simple and empirically powerful. It obtains new state-of-the-art results on eleven natural language processing tasks, including pushing the GLUE score to 80.5% (7.7% point absolute improvement), MultiNLI accuracy to 86.7% (4.6% absolute improvement), SQuAD v1.1 question answering Test F1 to 93.2 (1.5 point absolute improvement) and SQuAD v2.0 Test F1 to 83.1 (5.1 point absolute improvement).
papers.headline: 左右の文脈を同時に学ぶBERT、多様な言語理解課題へ少ない変更で適応
papers.summary: 質問応答や文の意味関係の判定に広く使える言語表現を得るため、文脈を処理するニューラルネットワークTransformerを用いたBERTを提案します。正解ラベルのない文章から左右両方の文脈を全層で同時に学びます。事前学習後は出力層を一つ追加して課題別に調整し、11の自然言語処理課題で当時の最高性能を報告しています。

papers.advantages: arXivの概要で比較する近年の言語表現モデルとの違いは、すべての層で左右の文脈を同時に条件として事前学習する点です。著者は、課題ごとに構造を大きく変更せず、出力層を一つ追加するだけで幅広い用途へ調整できるとしています。実験では11の自然言語処理課題で当時の最高性能を報告しています。ただし、比較した個々のモデル名や、各要素の効果を切り分ける実験はarXivの概要に示されていません。
papers.method: まず、正解ラベルのない文章を入力し、各位置の左右両方の文脈を全層で参照する表現を事前学習します。BERTは、この深い双方向の表現を学ぶモデルです。次に、質問応答や言語推論などの課題に合わせて出力層を一つ追加し、モデルを微調整します。共通の言語表現を利用することで、課題ごとの大幅な構造変更を避けられます。具体的な事前学習の問題設定やデータ構成はarXivの概要にありません。
papers.evaluation: 11課題で評価しています。複数の言語理解課題をまとめたGLUEは80.5%で7.7ポイント改善、文同士の意味関係を判定するMultiNLIの正解率は86.7%で4.6ポイント改善です。質問応答のSQuADでは、適合率と再現率をまとめたF1指標のテスト値がv1.1で93.2、v2.0で83.1でした。改善幅はそれぞれ1.5点と5.1点です。比較対象の詳細や学習条件はarXivの概要にありません。
